1.title: 3D Taylor–Green vortex
1.explore: Change grid size, backend and target iterations. Inspect velocity decay.
1.limits: Reference units. Use this small case to check installation and backend selection.

2.title: 2D Taylor–Green vortex
2.explore: Change grid size and target iterations. Compare the same physical time.
2.limits: Reference units. This is a planar numerical benchmark.

3.title: Taylor–Green vortex / TRT
3.explore: Compare the TRT collision model with example 02 at matching settings.
3.limits: Reference units. Collision models can have different stability limits.

4.title: 2D vortex / Smagorinsky
4.explore: Change grid resolution and compare decay with example 02.
4.limits: Reference units. Subgrid modelling does not replace a grid study.

5.title: 3D vortex / Smagorinsky
5.explore: Compare this 3D case with example 01 at matching settings.
5.limits: Reference units. Begin with a small grid and increase it gradually.

6.title: Driven cavity
6.explore: Run the cavity and inspect the recirculation pattern.
6.limits: Reference units. Wall-adjacent fields require grid refinement.

7.title: Forced channel flow
7.explore: Inspect the velocity profile across the channel.
7.limits: Reference units. Compare profiles after the flow has settled.

8.title: Wind around a block
8.explore: Edit domain, closed mesh, grid spacing and physics. Inspect slice and flow lines.
8.limits: Geometry uses metres. Demonstration viscosity is not atmospheric air.

10.title: Responsive hull search
10.explore: Enable evaluation and Run search. Pause holds the current candidate; disabling cancels. Hull geometry is an editable assembly of native GH expressions, points, mesh faces, volume measurement and transforms. Replace it with your own mesh; no Hawa hull node is required.
10.limits: Single fluid, submerged hull. No waves or buoyancy. Short scores demonstrate search; they do not establish an optimum.

11.title: 3D field visualization
11.explore: Use the shared snapshot to compare planes, tubes, contours and isosurfaces. Change field and colour map.
11.limits: Use one snapshot for comparisons. Keep colour ranges fixed when comparing cases.

12.title: Local airfoil and RC wing
12.explore: Choose an offline NACA code or local coordinate file. Edit wing span/chord. Load your own local polar.
12.limits: The bundled polar is synthetic format data. Lifting-line results assume attached flow; stall is not predicted.

13.title: Record and replay
13.explore: Choose a new absolute output directory. Start Record, wait for completion, then change Frame.
13.limits: Recording creates files. Use a new directory for each run. Playback must use the returned manifest.

14.title: Stationary curved sphere
14.explore: Connect a closed solid Brep to S on Hawa Geometry. Its surface approximation follows Cell size; W enables stationary wall interpolation. Compare cell sizes. The separate mesh supplies display and surface sampling only. Hawa Slice shows wall-clipped pressure; the hidden Plane Field remains available for a conservative-mask comparison.
14.limits: A smooth body needs resolved cells and gaps. Grid Preview remains a voxel diagnostic; interpolation places walls between sites. Do not combine these stationary links with refinement or moving bodies.

15.title: Fixed refinement patch
15.explore: Edit the domain and interior patch; run both grids and compare their field planes.
15.limits: One fixed 2:1 BGK patch. Keep interpolation stencils in fluid. No automatic adaptive mesh.

16.title: Cylinder wake recording
16.explore: Set a new absolute directory, then record the wake. Pause/resume or cancel. Replay saved frames.
16.limits: The full recording runs 8000 steps. Use a smaller trial first. Outlet and domain size affect the wake.

17.title: Oscillating cylinder
17.explore: Set travel amplitude in metres. Run the case; inspect the shared field snapshot and moved body.
17.limits: Prescribed motion, uniform BGK. Keep the full trajectory two cells from domain faces. Check grids and cycle averages.

18.title: Pitching airfoil
18.explore: Edit the offline NACA section and wing. Set pitch amplitude in radians; run and inspect loads.
18.limits: Coarse thick-foil demonstration. RC boundary layers are not resolved. Motion does not respond to fluid forces.

19.title: Rotating paddle
19.explore: Set RPM and run. Inspect body pose, torque and signed fluid power.
19.limits: Single fluid. No water surface, cavitation or free-body response. This is not a validated propeller model.

20.title: Completed-cycle motion search
20.explore: Run search. Each amplitude is evaluated only after settling and complete measured cycles. Pause or cancel as needed.
20.limits: Default objective is input power. Compare longer settling, more cycles and finer grids before ranking designs.

24.title: Boundary flow transfer between uniform grids
24.explore: Record a coarse parent block wake, map its time-varying velocity onto a finer child inlet, then run the child. Set new absolute recording and boundary paths. Enable controls in order: Record parent, Capture inlet, Run child. Parent 60 steps and child 120 steps cover the same physical duration.
24.limits: Experimental equilibrium velocity inlet; periodic transverse faces only. Demonstration viscosity. Quality checks sampled Mach/density; they do not prove convergence or atmospheric accuracy. Missing/solid samples, backflow, stale hashes and time extrapolation are rejected.

25.title: Profile inflow, resolved walls and open outlet
25.explore: Six Boundary Patch objects feed Boundary Set. X- uses a parabolic peak velocity of 1 m/s; Y walls meet its zero edge values. X+ is open and Z periodic. Wait for ready, enable Run, inspect the fixed blue-green field and quality report.
25.limits: Stationary uniform-grid NEE; approximate open boundary. Corrected smagorinsky-v1 is explicit. This short run demonstrates composition, not a converged or atmospheric result. Incompatible edge velocities are rejected.

26.title: Bidirectional flow on Y faces
26.explore: Y- and Y+ use open conditions with specified incoming exterior velocities. Initial velocity on Boundary Set is (0,-0.2,0) m/s. Pause, change it to (0,0.2,0), then run the new case to reverse the demonstration. Other faces are periodic.
26.limits: Open conditions switch using the interior normal velocity: incoming velocity or outgoing pressure. They can reflect disturbances. Adjacent open faces are not qualified. No atmospheric turbulence or rough-wall model.

27.title: Closed solid crossing a domain boundary
27.explore: A closed box extends beyond X-. Geometry classifies the full body inside the computation window. Boundary Set applies velocity to remaining fluid face nodes and preserves solid occupancy. Run and inspect the wireframe, geometry and field.
27.limits: Stationary voxel body, uniform lattice. Solid reconstruction donors and curved-wall/NEE overlapping nodes reject before solving. This demonstrates cropped occupancy; it does not qualify arbitrary building cuts or narrow gaps.

28.title: Experimental neutral rough-floor precursor
28.explore: Air viscosity is 1.5e-5 m2/s; reference wind is 5 m/s at 6 m. Change the z0 [m] slider (initial .01 m). X/Y are periodic; ground and lid lie half a cell outside the Z lattice planes. Wait for preparation, then enable Run. Compare equal physical time and wall traction.
28.limits: Unvalidated research model; transfer disabled. Startup log-profile drift is documented in the earlier review. A longer, filtered-wall case passes bounded stationarity checks; see docs/neutral-coupling-review.md. This short example is not developed atmospheric turbulence. No buildings, thermal stability, waves or currents.

29.title: Experimental roughness sensitivity
29.explore: Air viscosity is 1.5e-5 m2/s; reference wind is 5 m/s at 6 m. Change the z0 [m] slider (initial .1 m). X/Y are periodic; ground and lid lie half a cell outside the Z lattice planes. Wait for preparation, then enable Run. Compare equal physical time and wall traction.
29.limits: Unvalidated research model; transfer disabled. Startup log-profile drift is documented in the earlier review. A longer, filtered-wall case passes bounded stationarity checks; see docs/neutral-coupling-review.md. This short example is not developed atmospheric turbulence. No buildings, thermal stability, waves or currents.

30.title: Neutral rough ground and cropped buildings
30.explore: The left closed building extends through X-. Geometry classifies its full body and one-cell halo. Six patches feed Neutral Flow: neutral-profile X- inlet, X+ open, periodic Y, rough Z- ground and open Z+ top. Change the boxes, roughness, sampling plane or filter time. Run 1000 steps on MPS; Run false pauses.
30.limits: Experimental external flow at molecular air viscosity. One writer owns each incoming link. Stationary voxel buildings; rough floor only. Open faces can reflect disturbances. Uniform or neutral profiles; imported time series and curved links are unsupported. Finite low-Mach fields do not establish city-wind accuracy; transfer is disabled. Ground is z=0, half a cell below the first sample. Read docs/neutral-coupling-review.md.

31.title: Wind tunnel, probes and checkpoints
31.explore: Use metres in Rhino. Replace the closed mesh; Wind Tunnel sizes and orients its domain. Set Initialize runtime if needed, then Run. Probes sample pressure and velocity; Vectors draws the measured velocity. Pause before a file action. Set an absolute .npz path, choose save, load or export on Checkpoint, then toggle Execute off and on.
31.limits: A short CPU demonstration at viscous conditions, not an aerodynamic accuracy result. Checkpoint load requires the same case. Saving checkpoints pauses the solver. Execute is a rising-edge action and opens idle. Probe points must remain in fluid. Wind Tunnel uses Rhino document units; physical wind speed is m/s.

32.title: Translation, recording and particle paths
32.explore: A closed mesh translates along Y at 0.05 m/s. Set a new absolute directory, then Record. After 40 steps, use the Frame index slider to view body pose. Particles integrates through frames 0 to 4 and draws three fluid paths. Edit Translation to set direction, speed and startup ramp; choose a new directory for another recording.
32.limits: Prescribed motion, uniform BGK and a single fluid. The body must stay clear of the domain boundary. Coarse short demonstration, not a force validation. Particle trails use changing recorded fields; they differ from steady flowlines. Record false cancels; Pause holds the job. A saved true switch opens idle.

33.title: Neutral city → neighbourhood → pond
33.explore: Enable the five Record/Capture controls after opening idle. Each waits for its upstream data. Three grids share closed buildings, velocity, pressure, strain and compatible starting state. Move the shared slice height; the finest containing domain supplies the display. Edit pond roughness and inspect quality/statistics.
33.limits: Short transfer demonstration; atmospheric/nested statistical qualification still fails. Use new paths and retain parent files. Pond capture skips the first 0.369504 s of neighbourhood startup; its 1792 steps and frame 56 align the final absolute time. Match duration and playback when changing physics/time windows. Display trims halfway solid cells; raw samples retain conservative validity. No waves, currents or buoyancy.
